transcript.text: My Hotpoint washer dryer isn't drying properly any more and there's a funny smell when it's on the dry bit. Is there something I should clean?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Yes, there is most likely something to clean first. That 'funny smell' combined with poor drying on a Hotpoint washer-dryer is very commonly caused by fluff and lint building up where it shouldn't be. When the airflow is restricted because the filters are blocked, the air inside gets too hot and can scorch the trapped fluff, creating that burning or musty smell. It also means the moisture can't escape properly, so your clothes stay damp even though the machine thinks it's working hard. Before we look at any internal parts, please do these two checks:
1. Clean the lint filter: This is usually found inside the door opening (on a rim) or behind a small flap at the bottom front of the machine. Remove it and wash off all the fluff under warm water. Let it dry completely before putting it back.
2. Check the condenser: If your model has a removable condenser unit (often accessed via a panel near the filter), remove it and rinse it thoroughly to clear out any hidden lint. Also, please check how much laundry you put in for drying. Washer-dryers have a smaller capacity for drying than washing—usually about 5-6kg compared to an 8-10kg wash load. If you put a full wet wash straight onto the dry cycle, it simply won't dry properly and will generate excess heat/smell. Once you've cleaned those parts and tried a smaller load, let me know if the smell and drying issue persist.

Ok, unplugged it. I didn't know the filter needed cleaning, so I've never done it. I usually dry a full 8-9kg wash load straight after washing. The smell is like burning dust or scorched fabric, and the top of the machine gets very hot. I've still been using it though. I don't know if mine has a condenser.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Because the machine gets very hot and smells of burning dust or scorched fabric while drying, this is a safety hazard. Please do not use the appliance again until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. The most likely cause is that fluff has built up in the lint filter or condenser (or both), restricting airflow. When air can't flow freely over the heating element, the trapped fluff scorches and creates that smell, and the heat builds up inside the cabinet. The excessive heat may also have tripped a safety thermal cut-out or damaged the heater element itself. While you wait for an engineer to visit, please keep the machine unplugged. If you are comfortable doing so safely (with the power off), you can clean the lint filter and pump filter at the bottom front of the machine to remove any loose fluff, but do not attempt to open any panels or touch internal components. Once a qualified engineer has inspected it, they will be able to clear any blockages and replace the faulty part if needed.

candidates: Blocked lint filter or condenser causing restricted airflow and scorching fluff smell (high)
Overloaded drum for the drying cycle (medium)
Faulty drying heater element or thermal cut-out (low)
